# Get My Time (GMT)

> Get My Time (GMT) is a free-to-start app for Android and iPhone that helps you scroll less: it adds a 10-second pause before a limited app opens, shows your screen time as money and days of your year, and stops the app at your daily limit until midnight. No account is needed and your data stays on your phone.

- Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tritle.getmytime
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6823900088
- One link for both phones: https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/get/
- No account. No ads. Your data stays on your phone. Made by one developer in Thailand. On Google Play and the App Store.
- The app screens are in English; the site is in English and Thai.

## Sand (free) and Golden Sand

- Apps you can limit: Sand 2; Golden Sand 10
- Daily limit for each app: Sand up to 2 hours; Golden Sand up to 4 hours
- A 10-second pause before a limited app opens: Sand yes; Golden Sand yes
- Time is up at your limit, until midnight: Sand yes; Golden Sand yes
- Your time shown as money and days of your year: Sand yes; Golden Sand yes
- Share your progress: Sand yes; Golden Sand yes
- My progress: Sand last 7 days; Golden Sand all days
- Why you open apps: Sand a count; Golden Sand every reason
- Badges and streak: Sand some; Golden Sand all
- Block an app for hours or on a schedule: Sand -; Golden Sand yes
- Break reminder: Sand -; Golden Sand yes
- Export your data (CSV and PDF): Sand -; Golden Sand yes

## Prices (Thai baht; a store may show another currency)

- Sand: Free
- Golden Sand, Monthly: ฿39 a month (฿49 on iPhone)
- Golden Sand, Yearly: ฿399 a year

## Questions answered

- [Get your evenings back.](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/): Lost another hour to the scroll? GMT gives you a 10-second pause, shows what the time costs, and stops the app at your limit.
- [How to stop doom scrolling](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/how-to-stop-doom-scrolling/): To stop doom scrolling, add a small pause before you open the feed and set a clear end to your time. You do not need strong willpower. You need a gentle stop in the way.
- [Where does my phone time go?](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/where-does-my-phone-time-go/): The fastest way to learn where your phone time goes is to look at one full day, app by app. Most of it goes into just two or three apps.
- [An app to limit TikTok, Instagram and YouTube](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/app-to-limit-tiktok/): Yes, Get My Time is an app that limits the time you spend on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook and other apps you pick. You set a daily limit, and the app stops at that limit.
- [How to stop scrolling at night](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/stop-scrolling-at-night/): To stop scrolling at night, pick a stop time and make the feed harder to reach in bed. A small habit change does most of the work.
- [How to use your phone less](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/use-your-phone-less/): To use your phone less, start with one app and add one small stop to it. Small, steady changes last longer than big rules.
- [An app blocker for Android and iPhone](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/app-blocker-android-iphone/): Get My Time is an app for Android and iPhone that limits the apps you pick, and with Golden Sand it can also block an app. It starts with a calm 10-second pause, not a hard lock.
- [Is there something better than the phone's own screen time tools?](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/more-than-screen-time-minutes/): Your phone's own tools are good at one thing: they show how many minutes you spent. Get My Time adds three more things: a pause, the cost of your time, and a stop.

## Blog (a short post every week)

- [Get your time back](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/): Short posts, a new one every week. Each one gives you one small step you can try today.
- [Days off fly by: don't give them to the feed](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/days-off-fly-by-dont-give-them-to-the-feed/): Pick one good thing for each day off before it starts. Keep the phone for people and maps, and give the feed a short window in the evening.
- [Let only the people you love buzz your phone](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/let-only-the-people-you-love-buzz-your-phone/): Most buzzes come from apps, not people. Turn those off and keep the buzz for the people you love. Then each buzz is worth picking up.
- [Short videos: one more, and the evening is gone](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/short-videos-one-more-and-the-evening-is-gone/): Decide what your evening is for before you sit down. Then make the next video a little harder to reach, and pick your minutes before you open the app.
- [Teens and phones: limits you set together](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/teens-and-phones-limits-you-set-together/): Sit down together. Let your teen pick the apps and the minutes. Then let a pause and a Time is up screen do the reminding, so you do not have to.
- [Parents: how to show your kids a calm phone habit](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/parents-show-your-kids-a-calm-phone-habit/): Kids copy what they see. So start with your own phone. Pick a few calm habits, say them out loud, and keep them yourself. Small and steady beats a big talk.
- [Limits you can keep: how to pick the right number](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/limits-you-can-keep-how-to-pick-the-right-number/): Start from what you use now, then cut about a quarter. Keep that number for one week. If it felt fine, cut a little more. A limit you can keep beats a strict one you break.
- [Phone in bed: how to stop the late-night scroll](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/phone-in-bed-how-to-stop-the-late-night-scroll/): Make the phone sleep somewhere else, and give your hands something to do. Add a short wind-down, and a daily limit for the apps that pull you. Small steps work better than one big rule.
- [The 10-second pause: why a short stop works](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/the-10-second-pause-why-a-short-stop-works/): Yes, it can. A 10-second pause gives you a moment to choose before an app opens. In that moment you can ask, "Do I want this right now?" Often that is enough.
- [What is 1 hour a day? More than 15 days a year](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/what-is-1-hour-a-day-more-than-15-days-a-year/): One hour a day adds up to 365 hours a year. That is more than 15 days. To find your own number, take your daily hours, multiply by 365, then divide by 24.
- [New Year goal: scroll less, how to make it stick](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/new-year-goal-scroll-less-make-it-stick/): Make the goal tiny and clear. Decide the hard moment ahead of time. Set your limits once, and if you slip, start again tomorrow.
- [Your phone on a holiday trip: how to look up](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/your-phone-on-a-holiday-trip-how-to-look-up/): Pick a few moments to enjoy with your eyes only. Take a few photos, then put the phone away. Post later, not right now. You will remember more of the view.
- [A gift for your people: your full attention](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/a-gift-for-your-people-your-full-attention/): Give them your full attention. Put your phone away for one hour, look at them, and listen. It costs nothing, and many people remember it longer than a thing you can buy.
- [Exam week: keep your phone from eating study time](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/exam-week-keep-your-phone-from-eating-study-time/): Put the phone out of reach, study in short blocks, and use the phone only as a break. Set your app limits before exam week starts, so the choice is already made.
- [How to put your phone down at the dinner table](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/put-your-phone-down-at-the-dinner-table/): Make the table a place where the phone does not sit. Pick one or two small rules, say them kindly, and give the people your eyes. A short pause before apps open can help you remember.
- [Black Friday scroll: how to shop less on your phone](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/black-friday-scroll-shop-less-on-your-phone/): Sale apps are built like feeds. Timers, low stock and a full cart keep you looking. A pause before you open and a daily limit give the choice back to you.
- [Take back the last 6 weeks of the year](https://tritle129-lgtm.github.io/get-my-time/blog/take-back-the-last-6-weeks-of-the-year/): Yes, you can. Six weeks is enough to change one phone habit. Pick one app, add a pause and a limit, and see what you get back.
